title: secp256r1 (P-256) P256VERIFY Precompile for FEVM
description: Adds a P256VERIFY precompile at Ethereum address 0x0100 to the FEVM for efficient ECDSA signature verification over the secp256r1 (P-256) elliptic curve, following Ethereum's EIP-7951 semantics while remaining interface-compatible with RIP-7212, enabling WebAuthn/passkey authentication flows on Filecoin.

storageProviders: No direct impact on storage provider operations. The precompile operates purely at the FEVM layer and does not affect proof-of-power, block production, or sector management.
clients: Users can authenticate transactions using passkeys, WebAuthn/FIDO2 credentials, and device secure enclaves, enabling passwordless key management for FEVM dApps.
Lowers the barrier for user identity authentication in FEVM applications and facilitates account abstraction patterns.
tokenHolders: No direct change to FIL token economics. However, supporting modern authentication methods and cross-chain interoperability may broaden Filecoin's application scenarios and ecosystem value.
applicationDevelopers: Developers can call the precompile at address 0x0100 for secp256r1 (P-256) signature verification, eliminating the need for expensive pure-Solidity implementations.
The precompile interface is fully compatible with Ethereum's EIP-7951/RIP-7212 (same address, 160-byte input format, same return values), significantly reducing cross-chain porting costs.

On valid signatures the precompile returns 0x…01; on failure it returns an empty byte array. The precompile MUST NOT revert under any circumstances — developers should handle return values accordingly.
Gas accounting follows FEVM's normal Wasm-instrumented instruction accounting (per FIP-0054), not Ethereum's fixed gas schedule for precompiles.
